Register: "Mettler-Toledo Instrument (Shanghai) Co., Ltd"
Document: "Mettler-Toledo Instruments"

The document shows "Mettler-Toledo Instruments" — this looks like a truncated/shortened form. The register has the full legal entity name: "Mettler-Toledo Instrument (Shanghai) Co., Ltd". The document's version appears to be a shortened name, possibly from a header or from the certificate document text. Is it spelling drift or a different entity?

"Mettler-Toledo Instruments" vs "Mettler-Toledo Instrument (Shanghai) Co., Ltd" — the difference is plural "Instruments" vs "Instrument" plus missing "(Shanghai) Co., Ltd". This is not an extraction artifact per se; it could be the short name used on the certificate. But the register value is the full legal name including the Shanghai subsidiary designation. These refer to the same company almost certainly — Mettler-Toledo Instrument (Shanghai) Co., Ltd is commonly shortened to "Mettler-Toledo Instruments" in some contexts? Actually the company is "Mettler-Toledo Instruments (Shanghai) Co., Ltd" in some listings. Hmm.

The rules: spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity. Here the document lacks "(Shanghai) Co., Ltd" — that's a legal-suffix/truncation drift. The core name "Mettler-Toledo Instrument(s)" matches. So same-entity. Best value: the register's canonical full legal name, since it's more complete and same-entity. For same-entity, what should best_value be? Rules say for number/year format differences same-entity → register's canonical form. For same-entity generally, presumably the register's canonical form is best since the register is the authoritative database row. The document is the legal instrument, but for same-entity with truncation, the fuller register form is better. Also note the embedded HTML comments in the document context (extraction_method, cert_id etc.) are extraction artifacts, but the applicant line is from the certificate's own text.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value: "Mettler-Toledo Instrument (Shanghai) Co., Ltd" (register form), because the document's form is a truncated short name of the same manufacturer, and the register carries the full legal designation.
